text: The 'May/June 2021 Flood Repairs' initiative was a coordinated, multi-agency effort in New Zealand to address the severe flooding that occurred in late autumn and early winter of 2021, particularly in the South Island. The initiative involved systematic post-event residential building damage assessments and evidence-led methodologies to prioritize and accelerate repairs. It utilized supervised learning models to predict damage and support decision-making, and involved various public organizations in a collaborative framework to manage emergency responses and repairs.
